boundary: a stock node's own log, relaying broadcasts we transmitted at varying power

provenance.transmitter: Heltec V3 running our heltec_v3_sniffer, TX power swept +14..-9 dBm via a PWR command added for this measurement
provenance.observer: Heltec V3, stock Meshtastic 2.7.26.54e0d8d, US/LongFast, ~3 m away
provenance.method: 27 broadcast NodeInfo frames, each with a distinct packet id to defeat duplicate suppression. The node logs 'rx_snr found. hop_limit:N rx_snr:X' and 'Setting tx delay:Y' each time it relays; pairs were read from its own output.
provenance.note: Our two nodes, our own frames. No third-party traffic. Publishable under docs/TESTING.md.
provenance.clean_room_note: Black-box observation of the reference node's log. No reference source was read.

primary_axis_failed.intent: vary receive SNR to measure how the contention window scales with it
primary_axis_failed.result: FAILED. 23 dB of transmit power moved reported SNR by 1.25 dB (5.50 to 6.75).
primary_axis_failed.why: At ~3 m the link is far too strong. Even at -9 dBm the received level is roughly -46 dBm against an SF11/BW250 sensitivity near -134 dBm - about 88 dB of margin - so LoRa's reported SNR sits at its ceiling regardless of transmit power.
primary_axis_failed.what_would_work: Real attenuation (fixed pad or much greater separation), not a power setting. Until then the SNR SCALING of the window is unmeasured.

findings.claim: The transmit delay is a RANDOM DRAW, not a deterministic function of SNR.
findings.evidence: 33 samples across a 1.25 dB SNR span produced delays from 644 to 3976 ms, a 3332 ms spread. A deterministic mapping cannot produce that at fixed input.
findings.status: SETTLED. This was the specific ambiguity a single earlier sample could not resolve.

findings.claim: Delays are quantised to the 28 ms slot time.
findings.evidence: All 33 delays are exact integer multiples of 28 ms, with no exceptions.
findings.status: SETTLED. Confirms the window is counted in slots, and that the slot time the node reports is the quantum actually used.

findings.claim: At roughly 6 dB SNR the window reaches at least 142 slots.
findings.evidence: Observed slot draws span 23..142, mean 79.8, median 79, broadly uniform across the range.
findings.status: MEASURED AT ONE SNR ONLY. With 33 uniform samples the true upper bound is likely somewhat above 142; the low end of the window, at low SNR, is NOT measured because the SNR axis could not be varied.

consequence_for_our_implementation: code/protocol/routing.rs shipped ContentionWindow::MESHTASTIC_SHAPE with max_slots = 8. The measured window at high SNR is at least 142 slots - wrong by more than an order of magnitude. The documented DIRECTION was right; the scale was a guess and the guess was bad. Separately, slots_for_snr returned a deterministic wait, whereas the real behaviour draws uniformly within the window.

replication_2026_08_17.why: An independent second measurement, different session and different method. The original corpus was gathered by transmitting at varying power and reading a stock node's relays; this one harvested the reference's own 'Setting tx delay:N' log line while it relayed a third node's broadcasts. Nothing about the two shares apparatus, so agreement is evidence rather than repetition.
replication_2026_08_17.boundary: a stock node's own log line reporting the backoff it chose, while relaying broadcasts originated by a second stock node
replication_2026_08_17.agreement: max 4004 ms = 143.0 slots exactly, matching max_slots = 143 set from the first corpus.
replication_2026_08_17.what_it_does_NOT_settle: min_slots. All three nodes were within a few metres, so the SNR axis did not vary here either -- the same failure the original corpus records. Twenty-eight uniform draws from a single ~143-slot window land 16..143 exactly as observed, so the 448 ms minimum is a DRAW, not a window bound. Measuring the low-SNR end still needs real attenuation.
